clue.text: Board about to select place for the honoured guests

indicators.note: about here means turned around at one end, so the last letter of the word for select comes round to the front

parts.note: to select is to opt
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A company board is about to choose where the guests of honour will sit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a company's directors, but it is furniture; 'about' rotates the word for select, and 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: At a formal dinner the most important guests sit together at the head table, raised or set apart from the rest.

clue.text: Covering one on the roof with no sign of hesitation

indicators.note: with no means the word for hesitation is dropped from the roofer

parts.note: a roofer who lays straw or reed works on the roof
er is the sound a speaker makes while hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone up on a roof is putting on a covering without hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: The roofer is a THATCHER; 'with no' removes ER, the hesitation noise, leaving the material itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reed laid on a roof is a traditional covering for cottages.

clue.text: Literary collection of various parts up to prior, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the words before it are only one possible arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A monk's scrapbook of assorted bits, gathered up to a prior's standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides scented petals, the word is used for a medley or miscellany of writings put together.

clue.text: Acknowledge grant

definitions.meaning: to acknowledge a fact is to confess or concede it
to grant a point is to concede it

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean conceding that something is true, as in owning up to it.

clue.text: Restart for play with words not popular

parts.note: an actor's words are a line or lines
out of fashion, as in 'in' and 'out'

explanation.surface: Restarting a game of wordplay because it has gone out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, a LINE-OUT restarts play after the ball goes into touch: the forwards line up and the ball is thrown in between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union restart taken when the ball has crossed the touchline.

clue.text: Argue against the goal

definitions.meaning: to argue against is to protest or oppose
the goal of an exercise is its aim or purpose

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to protest; as a noun it means an aim or purpose.

clue.text: Pieces extracted from The Old Curiosity Shop?

definitions.text: Pieces extracted from The Old Curiosity Shop?

parts.words: Pieces extracted from The Old Curiosity Shop?
parts.note: pretends to mean passages quoted from the Dickens novel, but means the oddments a curio shop sells

explanation.surface: Excerpts lifted from Dickens's novel The Old Curiosity Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Small ornaments and curios of little value are the stock of a junk or curiosity shop.

clue.text: Former decree that's absolutely correct

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
an act of parliament is a decree

explanation.surface: An old decree that is completely right.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise and accurate in every detail, so correct without any margin of error.

clue.text: It shows nerve yet merit is out of order

indicators.note: out of order says the letters of these words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone shows cheek, yet their merit is improperly judged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve in the sense of rash boldness or cheek is a synonym.

clue.text: One from Athens clothed in some metal

indicators.note: clothed in means the Athenian is wrapped inside the word for some

parts.note: some means any, as in 'have you any?'
Timon of Athens is the title character of Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A Greek dressed in some kind of metal armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One from Athens' looks like a generic Greek, but it names Shakespeare's Timon of Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: The element, symbol Sb, is a brittle silvery metalloid often loosely called a metal.

clue.text: Sir, mad, upset, is to calm down?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Is it right that an angry knight should be calmed down?
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone is to allay their hostility or suspicion, calming them.

clue.text: Unusual second announced by the bookmaker?

parts.note: odd means unusual or strange

explanation.surface: A bookie calls out something strange for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker announces the prices or betting chances offered on each runner.

clue.text: Authority to strike

definitions.meaning: authority as in power or influence
to strike someone is to hit them hard

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both influence or pull, and to hit someone with the hand.

clue.text: Star model represented -by him?

indicators.note: represented means presented again, here with the letters arranged anew

explanation.surface: A famous model being painted by a great artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'him', the painter who represents the star model in a picture; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A great European painter of the period before about 1800 is the man who might portray a model.

clue.text: Certain timers can be put on after taking note

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Certain timers can be put on after taking note' (6) for PRESET: no parse found gives the P (SET for put, RE for note leaves P unexplained); likely OCR garble, and no source found for the printed text
annotationWithheld.clue: Certain timers can be put on after taking note

clue.text: The WI's now revising a Christmas production, perhaps

indicators.note: revising means reworking, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: The Women's Institute is reworking its festive pantomime script.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's community organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime based on the fairy tale is a classic British Christmas show.

clue.text: Ref is wrong in match an excessive amount

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the word for match

parts.note: to suit something is to match it

indicators.note: is wrong says the letters of the word before are wrongly placed

explanation.surface: The referee gets things wrong during a game, and makes far too much of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus or overabundance, more than is needed.

clue.text: Public school pupils should like them -as would the paying parents?

definitions.text: Public school pupils should like them -as would the paying parents?

parts.words: Public school pupils should like them -as would the paying parents?
parts.note: pupils would like gentle school terms, while parents paying fees would like payment by instalment

explanation.surface: Boarding school pupils want relaxed terms, and so do the parents footing the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: A British public school is a fee-paying private school, and its year is divided into terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment by affordable instalments, the deal a parent paying fees would welcome.

clue.text: Doctor to exist in unexciting surroundings. It'll take some lifting

indicators.note: in introduces the surroundings that the doctor and existing go inside
surroundings means the word for unexciting is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: dull means boring or unexciting
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: A doctor in a boring setting faces heavy work.
explanation.definitionFit: A short bar with weights at each end, lifted for exercise.

clue.text: Dress all the same

definitions.meaning: dress as in prescribed clothing worn by members of a group
all the same means identical or consistent throughout

explanation.definitionFit: A noun for standard clothing worn by a group, and an adjective for unvarying.

clue.text: You require power, they say, but not a lot

indicators.note: they say means the word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: might means power or strength

explanation.surface: You need strength, people tell you, but only a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount or a small thing, as in 'a mite tired'.

clue.text: Approach one at a r-rate

parts.note: a means one
the stutter on rate tells you to stutter its synonym cost, giving c-cost

explanation.surface: Going up to someone while stammering about a price.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed r-rate is a stuttered 'rate'; swap in its synonym cost and stutter that too.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them boldly.

clue.text: Island, for example, turns up in catalogue

parts.note: Arran is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An island, for instance, appears in a travel brochure.
explanation.definitionFit: To catalogue items is to arrange and classify them in order.

clue.text: Common cheat, he is ill-treated in class

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters sit inside the abbreviation for class

parts.note: cl is the abbreviation for class

indicators.note: ill-treated means roughly handled, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: A vulgar swindler, he is bullied at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' marks the slang sense: to chisel someone is to cheat them.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal slang the verb means to swindle or defraud someone.

clue.text: Deal with the plants after support in this dull place

indicators.note: after places the gardening task behind the support

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
to water plants is to tend them

explanation.surface: Doing the watering after propping up the plants in a sleepy spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiet stagnant place, away from where things happen.

clue.text: Tin containing the French polish

indicators.note: containing means the tin holds the French word inside it

parts.note: a tin is a can
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A tin holding French furniture polish.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish something is to make it bright and clean.

clue.text: A diplomat chooses part to agree with

indicators.note: part says only a portion of the words that follow is used

explanation.surface: A diplomat picks out which section to accept.
explanation.definitionFit: To match something is to correspond to it or agree with it.

clue.text: Worm wriggling about bit of earth seen in the garden

indicators.note: about means the jumbled worm surrounds the bit of earth
wriggling means twisting about, so the letters of the word are mixed
bit of here means just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A worm squirms in the soil of a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawnmower is a machine found in many gardens for cutting grass.

clue.text: It comes down as one goes out?

definitions.text: It comes down as one goes out?

parts.words: It comes down as one goes out?
parts.note: suggests a curtain or barrier, but 'goes out' means falling asleep or losing consciousness

explanation.surface: Something drops when a person leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin that closes over the eye drops down when one falls asleep.

clue.text: Lady to fight with opponents unexpectedly

parts.note: Una is a woman's name, the heroine of Spenser's Faerie Queene
war is a fight
in bridge East and South sit on opposing sides

explanation.surface: A woman takes up arms against her rivals out of the blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit as North-South against East-West, so E and S are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone unawares is to catch them by surprise, without warning.

clue.text: Window seen in the theatre?

definitions.meaning: a tall narrow pointed window in Gothic architecture
a surgeon's small knife used in an operating theatre

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a narrow pointed Gothic window and a sharp surgical knife.

clue.text: Manage praise left and right in retribution

indicators.note: manage means handle, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Handling compliments both ways as a form of revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of PRAISE gives EPRISA, flanked by R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A retaliatory act, punishment repaid in kind.
